fields.sample_size: official statements of the Swedish government and local authorities and reports (document corpus, size not stated); semi-structured interviews with two Ministry of Health and Social Affairs representatives, one Stockholm Municipality representative, and NGO representatives (two individual and one group interview at HEM; one at Civil Rights Defenders); participant observation in April 2016 at a language course (about 20 migrants) and one forest settlement near Farsta, Stockholm; critical discourse analysis
fields.effect_measure: critical discourse analysis of argumentation strategies; no quantitative estimate
fields.effect_estimate: The paper documents that homeless migrants in informal settlements receive little protection: police seize means of keeping warm, and municipalities do not always accept responsibility for access to water and sanitation; the study quotes Davies (2016), who found that most of 82 municipal eviction requests from public property were made on sanitation-hazard and littering grounds without providing facilities. Three themes dominate the authorities' arguments for not enforcing human rights law as migration prevention: public unease, equality before the law and integration in the country of origin; the author argues these legitimate harsh treatment and may be followed by zero-tolerance approaches as in Helsinki. Water and sanitation are one of several fundamental-rights issues (shelter, warmth, housing) and no water-access outcome is measured.
fields.section: Full text (8 pages): Introduction; framing of the hardship of the migrants; data and method (discourse analysis and interviews); analysis of arguments; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Section on friction points (shelter, water and sanitation, Davies 2016); Data and methods paragraph; Analysis; Nordic Journal of Migration Research 7(4):243-250

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative critical discourse analysis of official statements and interviews about the treatment of homeless Romanian migrants in Sweden, in which access to water and sanitation is one rights issue among several; read in full text 2026-10-04.
